Figure dimensions for a faceted plot

Source: R/panel-size.R
hv_panel_size.Rd

Chooses ggsave() dimensions from a plot's facet layout, so a faceted figure keeps panels of a readable size however many there are. A plot with one panel gets the standard 6 by 4 inch figure. A plot with several gets 3 by 2 inch panels, half the standard figure in each direction, plus the space its axes, titles, strips and legend need, measured by hv_ggsave_dims().

Usage

hv_panel_size(
  plot,
  max_width = NULL,
  max_height = NULL,
  units = c("in", "cm", "mm")
)

Arguments

plot

A ggplot object. Faceted with ggplot2::facet_wrap() or ggplot2::facet_grid(), or not faceted at all. A patchwork is refused: its panels sit in nested tables the function cannot count.

max_width

The widest figure allowed, in units. NULL, the default, is 6.5 inches, a journal's text width, converted to units.

max_height

The tallest figure allowed, in units. NULL, the default, is 9 inches, converted to units; with the 6.5 inch width it fits a page.

units

One of "in", "cm", "mm". Default "in".

Value

A named list with elements width, height and units, shaped to splat into ggplot2::ggsave() via do.call(), as hv_ggsave_dims() returns.

Details

When those panels, with the gutters and interior strips between them, would make the figure wider than max_width or taller than max_height, every panel shrinks by the same factor, so each keeps its 3:2 shape. A panel narrower than 1.6 inches leaves no room for 12 pt tick labels, so below that the function stops: the facets do not fit on one page, and ggforce::facet_wrap_paginate() splits them across several. A paginated plot is sized by the one page it draws.

The panel block is measured, not the whole figure, because the chrome around it varies: a long axis title or a legend at the top would otherwise come out of every panel.

See also

hv_ggsave_dims(), which measures the chrome.

Examples

# \donttest{
p <- ggplot2::ggplot(mtcars, ggplot2::aes(hp, mpg)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point() +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~cyl)
dims <- hv_panel_size(p)
do.call(
  ggplot2::ggsave,
  c(list(filename = file.path(tempdir(), "facets.pdf"), plot = p), dims)
)
# }
